section274ReVerifiedAfterRepair.meaning: the Expert HazLenz engine is untouched by the repair

MO_2.rootCause: Two functions independently restated what the email channel required, and they disagreed. describeAlertConfiguration() required a recipient and a credential; dispatchOperationalAlert() additionally needed a SENDER and, when it was absent, supplied alerts@safety-insite.invalid rather than declining. The disagreement always resolved the same way — readiness claimed a channel that could not deliver. The deeper cause is that the requirement had no single owner: it was written twice, so it could drift, and it had.
MO_2.senderFallbackAfter: NONE — an absent or structurally undeliverable sender leaves the channel NOT_CONFIGURED with the sender named as the reason
MO_2.undeliverabilityRule: reserved TLD test — RFC 2606 .invalid/.example/.test and RFC 6761 .localhost/.local — applied to BOTH sender and recipient, rather than naming one retired string, so the next such address is caught too

senderSemanticsDecision.chosen: A — SHARED, with an optional override
senderSemanticsDecision.rationale: A v1 product with one verified domain should not ask its owner to verify two, and the owner chose one provider at §293 precisely so one configuration step serves monitoring and EM-2. OPERATIONAL_ALERT_FROM_EMAIL is OPTIONAL and adds no required configuration; it exists so the shared-sender decision stays reversible by configuration rather than by another code edit.

MO_2.describeDispatchParity: STRUCTURAL. resolveEmailChannel() is the single decision point and both functions are written in terms of it. Proven over all 24 configuration combinations: "claims configured" and "transmits" are the same predicate in every one, and no combination transmitted an undeliverable sender.
MO_2.dispatchEvidenceBehaviour: monitoring.alert_delivered (info) on acceptance, monitoring.alert_delivery_failed (warning) otherwise, carrying channel, which alert failed, the bounded outcome and the provider status. Both are BELOW error severity on purpose: the dispatcher acts only on error, so it cannot alert about its own failure through the channel that just failed.
MO_2.malformedResponseRationale: A 2xx whose body is not a provider acknowledgement is MALFORMED_RESPONSE rather than accepted. Treating an unreadable success as a success is MO-2 one layer down.
MO_2.containment: UNCHANGED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. The send is still launched and abandoned with respect to the customer request — never awaited — so an alert-provider failure still cannot delay a request or turn a succeeded operation into a 500. What changed is that the promise resolves into evidence instead of into undefined, on the microtask that previously discarded it.

healthReady.productDecision: status stays ready under DEGRADED: a third party mail provider having a bad ten minutes must not stop Safety InSite serving inspections.
healthReady.limit: The three states are proven at describeAlertConfiguration(). The controller is a direct projection of that state, verified by reading and by type-check rather than by live observation. §294 makes no claim about production /health/ready, which is unchanged and still reports NOT_CONFIGURED from the deployed build.

twoPlacesTheGateCouldHaveLied: It reads the REAL LOG STREAM, not the test sink. captureOperationalEventsForVerification returns BEFORE dispatchOperationalAlert, so a harness built on it exercises emission and never exercises alerting. An earlier draft of this gate had two cases passing that way, with the provider never called and a thrown provider error never reached. The harness intercepts process.stdout/stderr.write instead, so the full production path runs and the redaction case asserts against the exact bytes a log drain would receive.

The noise-policy cases drive the REAL ServerErrorAlertFilter rather than restating its >= 500 predicate. An earlier draft restated it, which made the case agree with itself no matter what the filter did — a vacuous axis recorded as coverage. Five real HttpExceptions at 401/402/404/400/409 now produce a rate count of 0, 0 events, 0 sends and five unchanged client statuses; five real 500s through the SAME filter instance produce exactly one service.error_rate_exceeded and exactly one send.
